- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp drops; adjust forecast downward by 5–15% for next 3–5 days.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >45), model often overreacts and forecasts continued rise; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.3 to 0.3), model underestimates mean reversion; add 2–5% upward bias for 3–7 day horizon.
- When true outcome shows strong downward trend after a high, model often lags; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead to match true drop.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast amplitude by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early part of forecast; add 3–8% upward bias for first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.5) and price is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days if price is trending upward.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.5), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
